analysis: Examined release-swift.yml (head 1-177), the release-provider.yml publish/stage segment (head 1069-1261), the two changelog entries and the docs/developer/test.md patch. The change removes dev publication from master pushes and manual dispatch. A master push now routes only to staging, gated by vars.STAGING_ENABLED. A dispatch with validation_only runs the dev lane with validation_only hard-coded true, so it never publishes. Prod stays gated on a tag or a prod dispatch with !validation_only, and the tag-gated prod signing identity is preserved. Workflow-level validation_only no longer lets a staging or prod dispatch silently become a published run, because the staging and prod `if` conditions now include !inputs.validation_only. This is a tightening. The reusable publish-release job (lines 1086-1201) is unchanged in the visible hunk: R2 and release-key secrets are resolved per environment, PROD_* and legacy secrets are empty unless the environment is prod, and the job downloads a digest-pinned artifact and publishes via provider-release-publication.py. No new secret exposure is visible there. Not verifiable from the supplied evidence, so the next pass should check them: (1) release-dev-branch.yml, resolve-provider-release.sh and verify_workflow_source, none of which are in this batch. The changelogs and docs claim that the dev-push gate requires a GitHub-verified commit on dev ancestry, that the dev environment is the only one admitted from a dev push, and that secrets are inherited with the job checking refs/heads/dev. Because `secrets: inherit` hands DEV_* and the Apple signing secrets to a lane triggered by pushes to the dev branch, branch protection and the source gate on dev are the main control and cannot be confirmed here. (2) The claimed final-app designated-requirement check in build-and-release. Related threat IDs: A-005, A-011, T-013 and T-034 (binary trust and release registry). Nothing in the visible diff is a concrete regression, but the unseen gate changes affect a security conclusion.
